subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP child-session parallelism and fix launch readiness, or intentionally gate/serialize rapid ACPX launches?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs treat different ACP child sessions as parallel-capable, so a global launch gate would be a compatibility/product decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve parallelism and prove launch readiness
options.body: Run a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude repro and fix the confirmed OpenClaw/ACPX/adapter launch boundary without changing the documented distinct-session concurrency contract.

options.title: Add an intentional ACPX launch gate
options.body: Serialize or throttle rapid ACPX launches, but update tests and docs to make the new concurrency behavior explicit.

options.title: Defer for fresh evidence
options.body: Keep the issue in needs-info/manual-review until a current reporter or maintainer smoke identifies the failing boundary.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism and prove launch readiness
recommendation.body: Run a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude repro and fix the confirmed OpenClaw/ACPX/adapter launch boundary without changing the documented distinct-session concurrency contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACPX runtime and startup work is closest to the unresolved launch-readiness boundary, while the product choice can route from there to ACP/core owners as needed.
